items.title: Ten Years On, Somalia's Lower Shabelle's Farmers Still Can't Go Home: A Decade of War, Land Disputes, and Aid That Never Reaches Far Enough
items.description: It was the latest wave in a displacement crisis that has been building in Somalia's Lower Shabelle region for a decade, and there is no sign it is reversing. Aadan Rooble knows the pattern well. He walked for part of the ten days it took him to reach Mogadishu after airstrikes made the decision for him — the farm his family worked in the village of Farxaano was no longer somewhere anyone could stay. His sons now find casual work when they can. He doesn't expect to go home. He's one of tens of thousands of farmers who have fled Somalia's Lower Shabelle region over the past decade, arriving in M
items.titleIt: Ten Years On, Somalia's Lower Shabelle's Farmers Still Can't Go Home: A Decade of War, Land Disputes, and Aid That Never Reaches Far Enough

items.title: North Africa: Egypt Declares Suez Canal Secure As August Revenue Surges to $567 Million
items.description: [Radio Dalsan] CAIRO -- Egypt's Suez Canal Authority (SCA) has declared the waterway safe, with maritime traffic flowing normally as August revenue rose 56.7 percent year-on-year to $567.1 million, up from $326 million in the same month of 2025. SCA Chairman Osama Rabie announced the figures during a ceremony in Alexandria marking World Maritime Day 2026, organized by the Maritime Transport Sector of the Ministry of Transport.
items.titleIt: North Africa: Egypt Declares Suez Canal Secure As August Revenue Surges to $567 Million

items.title: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu
items.description: NISA said its forces arrested 11 operatives linked to the networks, which were allegedly being prepared to carry out activities threatening security. The networks were dismantled during planned security operations conducted in Darussalam, Garasbaley, Kahda, Daynile, and Afgoye. NISA forces also seized weapons and other materials that the operatives allegedly intended to use in their planned activities. The operations are part of NISA's ongoing efforts to prevent Al-Shabaab and other terrorist groups from carrying out activities aimed at undermining security and harming the Somali people.

items.description: El Niño Climate Impact Outlook – Somalia – UN OCHA Somalia's El Niño Climate Impact Outlook warns of a credible risk of severe flooding during the October–December 2026 Deyr season, particularly along the Jubba and Shabelle river corridors, if El Niño strengthens alongside a positive Indian Ocean Dipole. items.title: Somalia's Federal Member States Aren't Defending Sovereignty — They're Defending Their Patrons - No One in This Fight Is Neutral
items.description: Puntland is furious at Türkiye. Jubaland is furious at Türkiye. Both have spent the past five weeks accusing Ankara of killing their own people. items.description: On Sunday, 13 September, at least three journalists and three media outlets reported they were affected by a fake memorialization campaign, account suspensions and content removals, leaving their platforms inaccessible to their audiences. items.description: Egypt has been walking a tightrope since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, joining mediation efforts while signalling solidarity with Gulf Arab partners under Iranian attack. items.title: North Africa: Egypt Declares Suez Canal Secure As August Revenue Surges to $567 Million
items.description: [Radio Dalsan] CAIRO -- Egypt's Suez Canal Authority (SCA) has declared the waterway safe, with maritime traffic flowing normally as August revenue rose 56.7 percent year-on-year to $567.1 million, up from $326 million in the same month of 2025. SCA Chairman Osama Rabie announced the figures during a ceremony in Alexandria marking World Maritime Day 2026, organized by the Maritime Transport Sector of the Ministry of Transport.
items.titleIt: North Africa: Egypt Declares Suez Canal Secure As August Revenue Surges to $567 Million
